title: Fifty years after Mao's death, China still grapples with his legacy
subhead: 'Mao's Fraught Legacy' (1/7). Mao Zedong, who died on September 9, 1976, founded the People's Republic of China and still casts a shadow over the country's political life. The Chinese Communist Party, whose power base Mao established, remains divided between loyalty to his myth and condemnation of his 'mistakes,' which led to the deaths of tens of millions of people.

title: European Commission pushes to simplify and 'Europeanize' public procurement
subhead: The reform aims to 'end the dominance of price as a criterion,' which in practice benefits Chinese products, explained Stéphane Séjourné, the European Commission's executive vice president. Public procurement across the EU amounts to €2.6 trillion each year, representing 15% of GDP.

title: Le Pen's RN expels policeman party member over racist remarks
subhead: France's far-right Rassemblement National has expelled a police officer party member filmed making racist comments with colleagues while on duty. The incident, footage of which was released Tuesday, comes as Marine Le Pen's party seeks to make its image acceptable to voters ahead of next year's presidential election.

title: 9/11, 'the most photographed event in history, paradoxically produced only a handful of images'
subhead: Twenty-five years ago, after the World Trade Center attacks, the same photos appeared everywhere. This was a result of media concentration at work in the US at the time, explains photography historian Clément Chéroux in an interview.

title: In this French city, social diversity in schools has almost disappeared
subhead: According to studies, the southern city of Perpignan is the most educationally segregated in France. It's divided between private schools, which rank among the most privileged in the country, and public schools, which, in almost every case, sit at the exact opposite end of the social scale.

title: Unprecedented drop in French students' performance echoes worldwide decline
subhead: Reading and maths scores for 15-year-olds in France have fallen to their lowest levels since 2000, mirroring trends seen in comparable countries. Among the reasons cited to explain this global phenomenon are attitudes toward learning, the role of digital technology, the lasting effects of the Covid-19 crisis and a lack of parental involvement. In France, significant social and gender inequalities persist.
